name: read-swc-derived-effective-level
description: A computed value on request: `derived: ["effective_level"]` at the `swc` layer adds to each component its effective safety level — the level it declares, else the highest level any requirement allocated to it carries, and `QM` where nothing allocates one. The value is the validator's own name-keyed effective level, the one the diagrams label each component with, and never a second formula; a component name declared twice resolves to its first declaration, as that answer does. One row per component (`rows: "one"`), at an explicit `form: "index"`, the value under `"derived"` as `{"level": ..., "rating": ...}` — `rating` the plain level (`B` for both `B` and `B(D)`).

context.summary: The base model with `ExampleSWC` declaring `asil: D`, `REQ_EXAMPLE_001` allocating ASIL B to both of the base's components, and a third component, `UnratedSWC`, linked by a requirement that carries no level. So the three rows show the three ways the level is answered: declared, derived from the allocation, and `QM` by default.
context.notes: A read takes no scope and writes no audit record.

expected.notes: `effective_level` applies at the elements of the `swc` layer alone: asked at another layer or at a member path it is `schema-violation`, never a blank. A `where` clause on `derived.effective_level.rating` keeps the components at a level, decompositions included (`B(D)` is rated `B`); a clause on `level` matches the exact spelling only.
